route: /style-board/ (the style board: module process:photo-cards, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: The previous review asked for wider side padding and it has not been applied: the cards still have about 20px (1.25rem) on each side, against about 36px above the title under the number badge, so titles and text sit close to the white outline.
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards use about 32px of padding on every side, so the content sits evenly inside the outline.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set padding-inline: 2rem on .block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step (patterns.css:605 still sets 1.25rem), and move the .process-step__marker left offset to the same 2rem so the badge stays over the title's edge.

findings.issue: Each stacked card still has about 50px of empty space under its last line (for example, card 01 ends its text near y 640 and its outline near y 690) against about 36px above the title, so every card looks bottom-heavy; this was reported before and the shots show it unchanged.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards use the same padding on every side, so the content sits evenly inside the outline.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set margin-bottom: 0 on .block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step > :last-child, so the card's own bottom padding (1.5rem) is the only space under the text.

findings.issue: The line above the cards, 'How size-by-size print placement works', reads as a heading (it has no full stop) but comes as a lead paragraph, so it renders at body size and regular weight, smaller and lighter than the bold card titles under it, and the section's hierarchy reads upside down (m7-steps' 'Care steps from our rash guard labels.' has the same problem on both widths).
findings.reference: The competitor's sections open with a bold heading above their cards, heavier than the card titles.
findings.fix: Site Factory should either give the block this line as its heading (block.heading, which renders as the h2 .process__heading) or rewrite it as a full lead sentence that follows on from the section heading it continues.
